result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.quotient_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Create a quotient graph from a node partition. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L12094-L12212){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.quotient_graph(partition) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Quotient graph](/assets/graphs/algo-quotient.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="On the left, a six-node graph whose nodes are partitioned into three groups of two by categorical color (orange, teal, violet), with edges both within and between the groups. On the right, the quotient graph: each color group has collapsed to a single large super-node, and the inter-group edges from the original graph become edges between the corresponding super-nodes." width="100%"} Each block (group of nodes) in the partition becomes a single node in the quotient graph. Edges between different blocks become edges in the quotient. Edges within the same block are removed. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [partition]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[list[int | str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of node groups. Each inner list contains node IDs or labels belonging to the same block. Every node must appear exactly once. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new quotient graph where each partition block is a node. Nodes are labeled `"block_0"`, `"block_1"`, etc. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [KeyError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If any node in the partition does not exist. [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a node appears in multiple blocks or if some nodes are missing. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} A quotient graph is what you get when you glue an equivalence relation onto a graph: each block of the partition collapses to a single new node, and any edge crossing between blocks becomes an edge in the quotient. Intra-block edges are discarded, so the quotient never carries self-loops regardless of how they arose. Every original node must appear in exactly one block; a validation pass raises `ValueError` otherwise. Weights come from the first inter-block edge encountered per pair, which is fine when weights encode capacity but worth reviewing when they encode length or cost. Nodes in the returned graph are relabeled `block_0`, `block_1`, and so on, matching partition order. Quotients power community-level analysis, hierarchical coarsening, and the algebraic view of graph homomorphisms. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Create quotient from community partition: ::: {#048a27ea .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph(directed=False) g.add_path_graph(6) # 1 -- 2 -- 3 -- 4 -- 5 -- 6 # Partition: {1,2,3} and {4,5,6} partition = [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]] quotient = g.quotient_graph(partition) # Returns 2 quotient.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#65134c9e .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Returns 1 (from edge 3-4) quotient.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 1 ``` ::: ::: Quotient from community detection: ::: {#4ccccd0a .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ec.Graph(directed=False) g.add_path_graph(20) # Build a simple graph # Detect communities (use return_dict=True to get dict) membership = g.cmty_louvain(return_dict=True) # Build partition from membership from collections import defaultdict communities = defaultdict(list) for node, comm in membership.items(): communities[comm].append(node) partition = list(communities.values()) # Create quotient graph showing inter-community edges quotient = g.quotient_graph(partition) # Number of communities quotient.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 9 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#75d61727 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Number of inter-community edges quotient.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` 8 ``` ::: ::: Using labels: ::: {#e79c20e6 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "D") ) # Partition by labels quotient = g.quotient_graph([["A", "B"], ["C", "D"]]) # Results in block_0 -- block_1 ``` :::
